editorial:
Imagine a world where thousands of bored and hopeful teenagers start joining a weird cult called the Planet People. They believe they are going to be whisked away to a better world, and they all gather at old stone circles to wait for it to happen. You get to follow Professor Quatermass, a grumpy but brilliant scientist who realizes that these kids aren't just confused; they are actually being manipulated by something not from this earth. The vibe is very eerie and feels like a warning about how easy it is to follow a crowd when you feel lost in life.

What really works here is the slow build-up of dread and the creepy feeling that something is very wrong. The acting is solid, though some of the old-school special effects might look a bit silly to you now. It is a slow burn, so if you like fast action, you might get restless, but the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy old-school sci-fi, you should definitely grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see the detail. Otherwise, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to experience this strange trip without spending too much.
endingExplained: You find out the Planet People weren't going to a paradise. Instead, an alien species was using the cult to grow a giant organic monster that would eat all of humanity. In the final scenes, Quatermass has to stop the creature from fully waking up. He manages to destroy the alien hive, saving the world from being consumed. It ends with a grim reminder that humans are often too trusting of the wrong people.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school alien mysteries and weird cult stories.
